description: Advanced briefs. Each builds on a core prompt (basedOn) and adds numbered, checkable requirements. Titles end in '(Advanced)' so generations save to their own folders.

prompts.title: Tower Defense (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js tower defense game on a grid-based map. Players place towers along a path to stop waves of enemies reaching the base. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work and be reachable in play.

Requirements:
1. A 16x12 grid with a fixed path from spawn to base. Ground enemies follow the path waypoints exactly and never cut across buildable tiles.
2. At least 4 tower types with distinct roles: single-target, splash damage with a visible blast radius, a slowing tower that tints affected enemies, and a long-range sniper with a minimum range.
3. Each tower has 3 upgrade levels that visibly change its model and raise its stats. Selling refunds 70% of everything spent on that tower, including upgrades.
4. At least 4 enemy types: fast and fragile, armoured (takes reduced damage from single-target towers), flying (ignores the path; only some towers can hit it), and a boss every 5th wave.
5. A per-tower targeting mode: first, last, strongest, closest.
6. 15 waves defined in a data table with rising difficulty, and a between-waves countdown the player can skip for bonus currency.
7. Hover shows a green or red ghost for placement validity plus the range ring. Clicking a placed tower opens a panel with stats, upgrade cost, sell, and targeting mode.
8. Pause and 1x/2x/4x speed. The simulation uses a fixed timestep, so the same inputs give the same outcome at every speed.
9. Lives, currency, and wave counter in a HUD; a victory screen after wave 15 and a defeat screen at 0 lives, both with restart.
10. Projectiles and enemies come from object pools, and the game stays smooth with 150 enemies on screen.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN; no other assets). No placeholder buttons: every displayed control must work.
prompts.notes: Watch for: flying enemies following the ground path or being hit by every tower; upgrades that change numbers but not the model; targeting modes that all behave the same; speed changes altering outcomes (variable timestep); sell refund ignoring upgrade spend; no boss waves; a new mesh allocated per projectile.

prompts.title: Cloth Physics Simulator (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js cloth simulation. Render a cloth that responds to gravity and wind and can be manipulated with the mouse. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Verlet or position-based dynamics cloth of at least 40x30 particles with structural, shear, and bend constraints, solved with several iterations per fixed substep.
2. Tearing: constraints break when stretched past a threshold set by a slider. Torn cloth renders real holes (the index buffer is updated, no stretched triangles).
3. Collision with a sphere and a box the user can drag around; the cloth drapes over them without passing through, even when moved quickly.
4. Self-collision using a spatial hash, with a toggle and a readout of collision checks per frame.
5. Wind with direction, strength, and noise-driven gusts, applied per triangle using its normal rather than as one uniform force.
6. Left-drag grabs the nearest particle by raycasting against the current deformed mesh. Right-drag cuts constraints along the stroke.
7. Pin tool: click to toggle any particle pinned. Presets for curtain (top row), flag (left edge), and hammock (two opposite corners).
8. Double-sided lit material with normals recomputed every frame, plus wireframe and constraint-stress heatmap views.
9. Pause, single-step, reset, and a stats readout of particles, constraints, substeps, and frame time.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN; no physics libraries).
prompts.notes: Watch for: raycasting against the rest-pose geometry so grabs miss; torn triangles still drawn stretched; wind applied uniformly ignoring normals; cloth tunnelling through the sphere when dragged fast; O(n squared) self-collision; normals never updated so lighting looks flat.

prompts.title: Solar System Orrery (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page Three.js solar system simulation of all 8 planets. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Planet positions come from Keplerian orbital elements (semi-major axis, eccentricity, inclination, longitude of ascending node, argument of perihelion, mean anomaly at J2000), solving Kepler's equation on each update.
2. A date display and a date picker. Jumping to a date places every planet where it was on that date.
3. Two scale modes: true-to-scale distances with exaggerated planet sizes, and compressed logarithmic distances. Switching animates smoothly.
4. Axial tilt and rotation period for every planet; Saturn's rings tilted correctly; Earth's Moon and Jupiter's four Galilean moons with correct relative periods.
5. Procedurally generated planet textures (bands for gas giants, continents and oceans for Earth). No image files.
6. The Sun is the light source with a glow; planets have a lit day side and a dark night side.
7. Click-to-focus that keeps following the orbiting planet, with orbit controls relative to it. Escape returns to the system view.
8. Info panel: radius, live distance from the Sun in AU, live orbital speed, period, and number of moons.
9. Time controls: reverse, pause, rates from 1 day per second to 1 year per second, and a 'now' button.
10. Orbit lines are correct ellipses with the Sun at one focus; the asteroid belt is instanced points.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: circular orbits centred on the Sun; uniform angular speed instead of solving Kepler's equation; the focus camera left behind as the planet moves; a distance readout that never changes; moons orbiting in the wrong plane; a date jump that doesn't change the configuration.

prompts.title: Fractal Explorer (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js 3D fractal explorer that raymarches fractals in a fragment shader on a full-screen quad. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Three fractals selectable: Mandelbulb, Menger sponge, and a Mandelbox, each with its own parameters as sliders.
2. Distance-estimated raymarching with a max-steps slider and a surface epsilon that scales with distance, so detail holds up close.
3. Lighting: soft shadows, ambient occlusion from the distance estimator, and a key plus fill light, each toggleable.
4. Progressive rendering: reduced resolution while the camera moves, refining to full resolution when it stops.
5. Two camera modes: orbit, and free-fly (WASD plus pointer-lock mouse look) whose speed scales with distance to the surface.
6. A cross-section plane with position and orientation controls; the cut face is shaded differently from the outer surface.
7. At least 4 palettes based on orbit traps, plus fog colour and a glow for near misses.
8. Bookmarks: save the camera and parameters to localStorage and restore them. The current state is also encoded in the URL hash and restored on load.
9. A screenshot button that renders and downloads a 2x resolution image.
10. HUD with frame time in ms, current max steps, and resolution scale.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: a fixed epsilon that turns close-ups to mush; progressive refinement that never kicks in; constant fly speed so the camera passes through the surface; URL hash not restored; a blank screenshot (drawing buffer not preserved); an unlit cross-section face.

prompts.title: Procedural Terrain Biomes (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page Three.js terrain generator using layered noise, with biome shading, sunlight, and a day/night cycle. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Chunked endless terrain (at least a 3x3 ring of chunks around the camera) that loads and unloads as the camera moves. Chunk generation runs in a Web Worker created from an inline Blob so the main thread never stalls.
2. Level of detail: distant chunks use fewer vertices, with skirts or edge stitching so no cracks show.
3. Biomes chosen from both height and a separate moisture noise map: at least beach, grassland, forest, desert, tundra, and snowy peaks, with blended transitions.
4. A simple droplet hydraulic-erosion pass, toggleable, that visibly carves valleys.
5. Instanced vegetation (trees and rocks) placed by biome and slope, never on steep slopes or under water.
6. An animated water plane with fresnel-style shading and shoreline foam where the water is shallow.
7. Day/night cycle with sun and moon, sky gradient, fog colour tied to time of day, and stars at night.
8. A seed input: the same seed always reproduces identical terrain and vegetation.
9. Sliders for noise scale, octaves, water level, and erosion strength that regenerate only on release, not on every input event.
10. Fly camera plus a minimap heightmap showing the camera position and heading.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: generation on the main thread freezing the page; cracks between LOD levels; vegetation floating, underwater, or on cliffs; Math.random breaking seed determinism; the water-level slider not affecting shoreline or vegetation; erosion that changes nothing visible.

prompts.title: Mini Planet (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js low-poly tiny planet with procedural trees, houses, and rocks, all built in code (no external models). This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. The planet is an icosphere displaced by noise into land and ocean, with flat low-poly shading.
2. Props are aligned to the local surface normal, never placed in water, and kept apart by a minimum spacing check.
3. A character walks the surface with WASD under gravity toward the planet centre; the follow camera keeps the planet 'down', including over the poles (use quaternions).
4. Day/night cycle with an orbiting sun; house windows light up at night and stars appear.
5. Clouds orbit at different speeds and darken the ground beneath them.
6. Click any prop to focus: the camera arcs around the planet (never through it) and a label shows the prop type.
7. Build mode: place new trees or houses on valid land by clicking, with a ghost preview aligned to the surface normal.
8. Toon shading with an outline pass, a seed input, and a regenerate button.
9. Save and load the planet (seed plus placed props) to localStorage.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: the character or camera flipping near the poles (Euler angles); camera transitions cutting through the planet; props in the ocean; a build ghost that isn't normal-aligned; no outline pass; night not lighting the windows.

prompts.title: Fractal Tunnel (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page Three.js abstract fractal tunnel ride with repeated geometric segments, colour pulses, and forward camera travel. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. The tunnel is built from segments recycled from a pool as the camera advances, so the object count stays constant however long it runs.
2. At least 3 segment styles (hex rings, twisting squares, subdivided fractal triangles) that cross-fade into each other over a 20-second cycle.
3. The camera follows a smooth curved spline through the tunnel, banks into turns without roll jitter, and never clips the walls.
4. Audio-reactive mode driven by the microphone or by a built-in beat synthesised with Web Audio. Audio starts only after a click, with a clear fallback message if the microphone is denied.
5. Colour pulses travel down the tunnel as waves instead of every segment flashing at once. A photosensitivity safe mode caps flashing at 3 Hz.
6. Bloom and subtle chromatic aberration post-effects, each toggleable.
7. Controls: speed, palette (at least 4), pulse frequency, twist amount, and a segment-style lock.
8. A seamless loop mode where one cycle ends exactly where it began, with no visible jump.
9. FPS counter and a readout of pooled objects in use.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: segments created forever instead of recycled; roll jitter when banking; safe mode that doesn't cap flashing; audio started without a user gesture; a visible seam at the loop point; bloom washing everything out to white.

prompts.title: Hologram Showcase (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page Three.js hologram product viewer with a pedestal, rim lights, and hotspot labels. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Three products modelled in code (for example headphones, a drone, a watch), switchable through an animated carousel.
2. A custom hologram ShaderMaterial: object-space scanlines, fresnel rim glow, flicker noise, and a vertical reveal sweep when a product appears.
3. Hotspots anchored to model-space points that stay attached while the model rotates and hide when the model occludes them.
4. Clicking a hotspot eases the camera to it and opens a detail card. Auto-rotation pauses during focus and resumes afterwards.
5. Exploded view: a slider separates each product's parts along defined axes, and hotspots move with their parts.
6. A reflective pedestal floor and animated light rings.
7. A colourway selector that changes hologram tint and emissive colour per product.
8. Keyboard access: Tab cycles hotspots, Enter focuses, Escape backs out. Card text meets WCAG AA contrast.
9. Responsive layout: on a portrait phone the detail card becomes a bottom sheet.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: hotspots visible through the model; exploded view leaving hotspots behind; scanlines in screen space instead of object space; auto-rotation fighting the focus transition; no keyboard navigation; carousel switches leaking geometries and materials.

prompts.title: Voxel Builder (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js voxel editor with raycast placement and grid snapping. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A 32x32x32 build volume stored in a typed array and rendered as merged chunk meshes with hidden faces culled, never one mesh per block. Only the edited chunk is remeshed.
2. Tools: place, remove, paint, box fill (drag two corners), line, and flood fill of connected same-colour voxels.
3. Undo/redo of whole tool operations (a box fill is one step), at least 100 steps.
4. Mirror symmetry on X and/or Z with a visible mirror plane; voxels on the plane are not doubled.
5. A palette of 16 editable colours plus an eyedropper.
6. The ghost preview shows exactly the cells the active tool will change, including box-fill extents.
7. Save and load named models to localStorage with a version field and validation, so corrupted data shows an error instead of breaking startup.
8. Export the model as a JSON file download, import one through a file picker, and export a PNG snapshot.
9. Per-vertex ambient occlusion for depth.
10. Readouts for block count and triangle count.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: one Mesh per voxel; undo storing each voxel of a fill as its own step; mirror applying twice on the mirror plane; remeshing the whole volume on every click; AO seams between chunks; import without validation.

prompts.title: Endless Runner Prototype (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js endless runner with procedural track chunks, obstacles, and collision. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Three lanes with smooth lane switching, jump, and slide, plus coyote time and an input buffer so inputs feel fair.
2. Track assembled from at least 8 authored chunk patterns chosen by a difficulty budget, recycled from a pool with no gaps.
3. Obstacles: low barrier (jump), high barrier (slide), full block (change lane), and moving obstacles that telegraph before switching lanes.
4. Coins plus two power-ups, magnet and shield, with HUD timers.
5. Speed rises with distance, and every chosen pattern is guaranteed passable at the current speed.
6. Hitboxes are separate from visuals, with a debug toggle that draws them; the slide hitbox is shorter.
7. Frame-rate independent movement: a 30/60/144 Hz simulation toggle covers the same distance in the same time.
8. A floating-origin reset keeps world coordinates small on long runs.
9. Title, pause, and game-over screens showing distance, coins, and a localStorage best. Restart clears all timers and pooled objects.
10. Touch swipe controls as well as keyboard.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: impossible patterns at high speed; power-ups surviving a restart; jitter after long runs (no floating origin); a slide that doesn't change the hitbox; no swipe controls; chunk gaps once speed rises.

prompts.title: DNA Sculpture (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page Three.js animated DNA double helix. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Correct helix geometry: about 10.5 base pairs per turn, antiparallel backbones, and visible major and minor grooves (strands offset by less than 180 degrees).
2. Base pairs coloured by type (A-T, G-C) from an editable sequence field. Invalid characters are rejected with a message, and the complementary strand is generated automatically.
3. Rendered with InstancedMesh for spheres and connectors, smooth with at least 2,000 base pairs.
4. Connectors oriented exactly between paired bases using quaternions.
5. Hovering a base pair highlights it and shows its index and pair; clicking pins an info label.
6. An 'unzip' slider that separates the strands progressively from one end, as in replication.
7. Controls for pitch, radius, rotation speed, and sequence length that update instance matrices instead of rebuilding geometry.
8. Three render styles: ball-and-stick, ribbon backbone (tube along a curve), and space-filling.
9. Camera modes: gentle orbit, fly along the helix axis, and a reduced-motion toggle.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: strands exactly 180 degrees apart (no grooves); rebuilding geometry on every slider tick; misoriented connectors; hover returning the wrong instance index; a wrong complement strand; unzip implemented as scaling.

prompts.title: Origami Fold (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js origami folding animation with a timeline. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A real crease pattern (for example a waterbomb base or crane base) defined as data: vertices, faces, and mountain/valley creases.
2. Folding is done by rotating face groups around crease lines as hinges, never by linearly morphing vertices.
3. A sequence of at least 6 labelled fold steps played in order.
4. Timeline scrubber, play/pause, step forward/back, and speed. Scrubbing to any time gives exactly the same state as playing to it.
5. Double-sided paper with different front and back colours and visible thin edges.
6. Crease lines drawn on the paper with distinct mountain and valley styles, visible when unfolded.
7. Stacked layers get small offsets so they never z-fight or flicker.
8. A wireframe overlay and a 2D crease-pattern panel that highlights the crease used by the current step.
9. Orbit camera plus a button that auto-frames the model for the current step.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: vertex lerping that passes paper through itself; scrubber and playback states diverging; flickering stacked faces; single-sided material showing holes; a crease panel out of sync with the step; steps out of order.

prompts.title: Sci-Fi Hangar Drones (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js sci-fi hangar with hovering drones, warning lights, emissive runway strips, and fog. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A procedural hangar: panelled floor, catwalks, support beams, and bay doors that open.
2. At least 8 drones using steering behaviours (separation, alignment, cohesion, obstacle avoidance) so they never intersect each other or the walls.
3. Formation modes (hover, grid, circle, V-shape, land on pads) reached by steering, never by teleporting.
4. Each drone has blinking nav lights and a thruster glow that scales with its speed.
5. Rotating warning beacons are real lights that illuminate nearby surfaces, kept to a sensible number of dynamic lights.
6. Light shafts and fog use soft, depth-faded particles or planes with no hard intersection lines.
7. Camera modes: a cinematic spline path with keyframed look targets, free orbit, and follow-a-drone.
8. Click a drone to select it: a HUD tag shows its ID, speed, and state, and clicking the floor commands it there while it still avoids others.
9. A bay-door sequence: alarm lights, doors open, drones fly out and return, and the scene resets cleanly.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: drones clipping during formation changes; too many dynamic lights or lights that don't reach surfaces; hard fog-plane intersections; jittery follow camera; a commanded drone ignoring avoidance; the bay sequence not resetting.

prompts.title: 3D Gravity Well Simulation (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create an interactive Three.js gravity well simulation with a deformable spacetime grid, placeable massive objects, and launchable particles. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. N-body gravity using a symplectic integrator (leapfrog or velocity Verlet) with a fixed timestep, substeps, and softening near masses.
2. Massive bodies can move and attract one another, with a 'fixed masses' toggle.
3. Grid deformation derived from the summed potential of all masses and computed efficiently (in the vertex shader, or on CPU at a sensible resolution).
4. Black holes with an event horizon: particles that cross it are absorbed and add to its mass.
5. Launch tool: drag to set a velocity vector while a predicted trajectory preview is integrated ahead with the same physics.
6. Presets: a stable two-body orbit, the figure-eight three-body solution, and a slingshot flyby.
7. Trails with a fixed maximum length stored in ring buffers.
8. Readouts for total energy and momentum showing how much they drift.
9. Select any body to edit its mass and velocity; the selected body is highlighted.
10. Time scale, pause, step, and reset.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: explicit Euler with runaway energy; a trajectory preview that disagrees with the real path; per-vertex-per-mass CPU loops on a huge grid; absorbed particles still drawn; an unstable figure-eight from wrong initial conditions; trails growing without bound.

prompts.title: GTA 6 Game (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a polished single-page Three.js open-world crime-action game inspired by GTA 6, set in an original neon coastal city. Use original procedural low-poly geometry only: no copyrighted logos, named characters, map data, audio, or ripped assets. The core game must include: a third-person character (WASD, sprint, jump, mouse camera, raycast shooting, health, enter/exit vehicles with E); arcade driving with collisions, durability, and a chase camera; a compact city with roads, varied buildings, beach, ocean, palms, neon areas, ramps, and landmarks; ambient traffic on roads and wandering pedestrians; a 0-to-5-star wanted system with pursuing police and a visible evade cooldown; a HUD with health, durability, cash, stars, mission text, prompts, and a rotating minimap; a sunset-to-night lighting cycle; title, controls, pause, game-over, and mission-complete screens. This is the advanced brief: on top of all of that, every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Five chained story missions with a mission select at the safehouse, failure conditions, and checkpoints.
2. At least 3 vehicle classes with different handling: sports car, motorbike, and boat (boats only on water).
3. A weapon wheel with melee, pistol, and SMG, each with ammo, reload, and pickups, plus an aim-assist toggle.
4. Police escalation per star: 1-2 patrol cars, 3 roadblocks, 4 a helicopter with a searchlight, 5 heavy units.
5. Traffic lights at intersections that NPC traffic obeys; pedestrians flee from gunfire and crashes.
6. In-vehicle radio with 2 stations of music synthesised with Web Audio, and engine sound that follows RPM.
7. Save and load to localStorage: cash, completed missions, owned vehicles, and player position.
8. Settings menu: mouse sensitivity, invert Y, and a graphics preset (shadows, draw distance, NPC cap) that applies live.
9. Fixed-timestep physics independent of frame rate, with object pooling for transient effects and capped NPC counts.
10. An F3 debug overlay with FPS, active NPCs, pooled objects, and draw calls.

Deliver one standalone HTML file with embedded CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN). No placeholder buttons, TODOs, or decorative systems: every displayed control and feature must work.
prompts.notes: Watch for: a static city with no working mission chain; entering vehicles or boats breaking player or camera state; boats driving on land; frame-rate-dependent driving; traffic ignoring lights; police escalation that stops at one car; wanted stars that never decay; a save that doesn't restore missions; settings that don't apply; the minimap in the wrong orientation; unbounded NPCs or effects tanking performance.

prompts.title: Audio-Reactive Visualizer (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page p5.js audio-reactive visualizer. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Input source selector: microphone, an audio file the user picks with a file input (nothing bundled), and a built-in demo track synthesised with Web Audio.
2. Real onset detection using spectral flux with an adaptive threshold (not raw volume), a visible beat indicator, and a BPM estimate.
3. Logarithmic frequency bands (bass, low-mid, high-mid, treble), each driving a different visual element.
4. At least 4 scenes: circular spectrum, waveform ring with particles, scrolling frequency terrain lines, and a kaleidoscope. Number keys switch scenes, and strong drops can auto-switch.
5. Per-band smoothing and gain controls, plus auto-gain that normalises quiet sources.
6. A pooled particle system with a hard cap.
7. Fullscreen toggle, hide-UI toggle, and a 10-second WebM recording of the canvas using MediaRecorder.
8. Clear on-screen messages for a denied microphone, an unsupported file, and a suspended AudioContext. Audio only starts after a user gesture.
9. A photosensitivity safe mode that limits flashing.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (p5.js may load from a CDN; no audio files).
prompts.notes: Watch for: beat detection that just thresholds volume; linear bands so bass dominates everything; a file input that never connects to the analyser; recording that saves an empty file; crashes when the microphone is denied; particles allocated without a cap.

prompts.title: Double Pendulum Chaos (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single-page p5.js double pendulum simulation using the real equations of motion. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. RK4 integration with a fixed timestep and substeps. Energy drift stays under 0.1% over 60 seconds with damping off, shown in a readout.
2. Up to 50 pendulums whose starting angles differ by 1e-6 radians, drawn with a colour gradient and staying smooth.
3. A live graph of angular separation between the first and last pendulum on a log scale, with an estimated Lyapunov exponent.
4. A phase-space panel plotting angle against angular velocity.
5. Parameters for both masses, both lengths, gravity, and damping; changes reset the simulation.
6. Drag either bob to set initial conditions; physics pauses while dragging.
7. A flip-time fractal mode: a grid of initial angle pairs coloured by time until the lower arm first flips over, computed progressively in chunks without freezing the page.
8. Fading per-pendulum trails that clear on reset.
9. Pause, step, speed, and an RK4/explicit Euler toggle that demonstrates Euler's energy blow-up.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (p5.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: RK4 claimed but Euler implemented; pendulums not diverging because they share the same start; a flip-fractal that freezes the tab; an energy readout that ignores potential energy; trails bridging across resets; a Lyapunov estimate that is a constant.

prompts.title: Pixel Art Editor (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a pixel art editor as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript, with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Layers: add, delete, reorder, rename, visibility, and opacity, composited correctly.
2. Animation frames on a timeline with onion skinning (previous and next frames tinted), an fps control, and preview playback.
3. Tools: pencil, eraser, line, rectangle and ellipse (filled or outline), flood fill (iterative; contiguous or global), eyedropper, rectangular selection with move, copy, and paste.
4. A pixel-perfect pencil mode that removes L-shaped corners from strokes.
5. Horizontal and vertical symmetry drawing.
6. Undo/redo per whole stroke or operation across layers and frames, at least 200 steps.
7. Palette import and export as .hex text, and palette swap that recolours every pixel of one colour.
8. Mouse-wheel zoom centred on the cursor and space-drag panning.
9. Export: PNG at a chosen scale, a sprite-sheet PNG of all frames, and an animated GIF encoded in the page by your own minimal GIF encoder.
10. Save and load projects to localStorage and as a JSON file.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: recursive flood fill overflowing the stack; undo storing every pixel of a drag as its own step; zoom that jumps away from the cursor; a GIF encoder that outputs a corrupt file or ignores frame timing; onion skin painted into the frame data; layer opacity lost on export.

prompts.title: WebAudio Synth Keyboard (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a playable synthesizer as a single HTML page using the Web Audio API and vanilla JavaScript, with no libraries or audio files. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Two oscillators per voice with waveform, octave, detune, and mix, plus a noise source.
2. 8-voice polyphony with voice stealing (oldest note first) and no clicks when a voice is stolen.
3. Separate amplitude and filter ADSR envelopes, filter envelope amount, and keyboard tracking.
4. An LFO with rate, depth, and destination: pitch, filter cutoff, or amplitude.
5. Effects chain: tempo-synced delay with feedback, convolution reverb using an impulse response generated in code, and chorus.
6. An arpeggiator (up, down, random; rate synced to BPM) and a 16-step sequencer that records played notes.
7. Web MIDI input when available (note on/off, velocity, pitch bend, mod wheel), with a message when unsupported.
8. Six built-in presets plus saving and loading user presets in localStorage.
9. Oscilloscope and spectrum analyser connected to the final output.
10. Arpeggiator and sequencer notes are scheduled on the AudioContext clock with a lookahead scheduler, not fired from setInterval.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript. Audio must start only after a user gesture.
prompts.notes: Watch for: clicks from voice stealing without a ramp; sequencer timing drifting because notes fire from timers; a reverb node with no impulse response (silence); MIDI code that throws when unsupported; analysers tapping before the effects; presets that don't restore every parameter.

prompts.title: Raymarched Mandelbulb (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page that renders a raymarched Mandelbulb in a full-screen WebGL fragment shader, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. WebGL2 with a clear on-page message if it is unavailable.
2. A distance estimator using the running derivative, with a surface epsilon scaled by distance.
3. Dynamic resolution that adjusts to hold a target frame time, shown in the HUD.
4. Progressive anti-aliasing: when the camera is still, jittered samples accumulate into a float framebuffer.
5. Lighting: soft shadows, ambient occlusion, a glow term, and distance fog, each toggleable.
6. A power slider (2 to 12) with a 'breathe' animation mode, and a Julia-bulb mode with an adjustable 3D constant.
7. Orbit and free-fly cameras built on quaternions, with no gimbal lock.
8. At least 4 orbit-trap palettes plus a custom 3-stop gradient editor.
9. Shader compile or link errors caught and shown in an on-page panel with line numbers.
10. A 2x resolution screenshot rendered through an offscreen framebuffer and downloaded.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: shader compile errors (still the most common failure); accumulation that never resets when the camera moves, leaving ghosting; dynamic resolution oscillating every frame; float framebuffers used without checking EXT_color_buffer_float; gimbal lock at the poles; blank screenshots.

prompts.title: Raymarched Clouds (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader rendering volumetric clouds, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Physically inspired lighting: Beer-Lambert absorption, a Henyey-Greenstein phase function with forward and back lobes, and a secondary light march toward the sun for self-shadowing.
2. A 2D weather map controlling coverage, with a slider blending between cumulus and stratus shapes.
3. 3D noise (Worley plus Perlin) generated once at startup into a 3D texture, never computed per sample.
4. Blue-noise or interleaved-gradient jitter on ray start positions so low step counts don't band.
5. A sky gradient that matches the sun position, with a sun disc and light shafts.
6. Time-of-day slider and an animate-day toggle; clouds pick up warm colours at dawn and dusk.
7. Mouse-look camera that can fly above, into, and below the cloud layer, and renders correctly from inside it.
8. Low, medium, and high quality presets that change step counts and resolution scale, plus an FPS counter.
9. Wind direction and speed sliders that move noise layers at different rates.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: flat noise with no light march (no self-shadowing); per-sample procedural noise collapsing the frame rate; black or broken image when the camera is inside the layer; banding with no jitter; a sun disc that disagrees with the lighting direction; quality presets that change nothing.

prompts.title: Procedural Fire (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page with a WebGL fire effect, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Fire is a 2D grid fluid simulated on the GPU with ping-pong framebuffers: velocity and temperature advection, buoyancy, pressure projection, and vorticity confinement. Not scrolling noise.
2. Colour from a blackbody-style temperature ramp, with smoke from cooled density.
3. Emitter presets (torch, campfire with several logs, steady candle) plus a paint mode that draws fire with the mouse.
4. Wind applied as a force on the velocity field so the flame bends and sheds.
5. Click to place solid circular obstacles the fire flows around.
6. GPU-instanced spark particles spawned from hot regions, with drag and cooling.
7. A heat-distortion post-effect over a background scene.
8. Sliders for fuel, buoyancy, cooling, vorticity, and simulation resolution; pause and reset.
9. Float render-target support is checked; fall back to a lower-precision path with an on-page note if it's missing.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: noise scrolling upward presented as a simulation; no pressure projection so the fluid gains mass; wind translating the flame instead of bending it; obstacles drawn but not enforced as boundaries; reading and writing the same texture; blank output on devices without float textures.

prompts.title: CRT Post-Processing (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page that renders a test scene and applies a CRT post-processing pipeline, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. The source is a small playable game (for example Breakout) rendered into a 320x240 framebuffer.
2. A multi-pass pipeline: scene, phosphor persistence feedback buffer, bloom downsample/blur chain, then the CRT composite.
3. Selectable shadow masks: aperture grille, slot mask, and dot triad.
4. Scanlines whose thickness depends on pixel brightness, aligned to the 240-line source rather than the display.
5. NTSC-style composite colour bleeding with a dot-crawl toggle.
6. Curvature with correct UV remapping, rounded corners, vignette, and a faint glass reflection.
7. An interlace flicker toggle and a sync wobble triggered by a 'channel change' button.
8. Presets: arcade monitor, consumer TV, studio monitor, and CRT off.
9. A draggable split-screen comparison of raw and processed output.
10. Settings persist in localStorage, and the pipeline handles resize and devicePixelRatio.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: effects applied to a black texture (scene never rendered into the framebuffer); scanlines aliasing with the display resolution; persistence smearing forever with no decay; curvature sampling outside the texture; a split view that shows the same image on both sides; framebuffers not resized.

prompts.title: Shader Game of Life (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page implementing Life-like cellular automata entirely on the GPU with ping-pong framebuffers, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A rule editor accepting any Life-like rule in B/S notation, with presets for B3/S23 (Life), B36/S23 (HighLife), and B2/S (Seeds).
2. Grid sizes up to 2048x2048 with a toroidal-wrap toggle.
3. Zoom and pan, with painting mapped to the correct cell at every zoom level.
4. A pattern library (glider, LWSS, pulsar, Gosper glider gun, R-pentomino, acorn) with rotate and flip before stamping, and a ghost preview under the cursor.
5. RLE import: paste standard RLE text and stamp it.
6. Cell age stored in a separate channel, with age palettes and a heat map of recent change.
7. A generation counter and a population graph read back occasionally, not every frame.
8. Speed from 1 to 64 generations per frame, plus single-step and pause.
9. Save and restore the grid to localStorage, compressing or downsampling large grids.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: reading and writing the same texture; neighbour sampling off by half a texel; wrap toggle ignored; mouse painting off after zooming; an RLE parser that ignores run counts or line ends; readPixels every frame killing performance.

prompts.title: Ocean Seascape (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a single HTML page with a full-screen WebGL fragment shader rendering an open ocean, writing all WebGL code in plain JavaScript with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A wave field summing at least 8 Gerstner waves driven by wind direction, with analytic normals.
2. Ray intersection with the displaced surface by heightfield marching with bisection refinement.
3. Lighting: fresnel sky reflection, scattered blue-green colour in thin wave peaks, and a sharp sun specular highlight.
4. Foam generated from wave steepness, accumulating on crests and fading.
5. Sky with sun, soft clouds, and horizon haze, plus a time-of-day slider.
6. A storm slider that shifts the wave spectrum, darkens the sky, and adds rain streaks and lightning flashes.
7. A floating buoy that bobs and tilts using wave height and normal computed in JavaScript from the same wave function as the shader.
8. An underwater view when the camera dips below the surface: fog, a caustic light pattern, and the surface seen from below.
9. Mouse-drag look and camera height, quality presets, and an FPS counter.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: bump-mapped flat water with no real displacement; a buoy that floats out of sync because JavaScript and GLSL wave functions differ; a missing fresnel term making the water look like plastic; foam everywhere; broken rendering below the surface; a horizon that bends at the screen edges.

prompts.title: Flappy Bird Clone (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a Flappy Bird clone as a single HTML page with vanilla JavaScript and canvas, drawing everything in code with no libraries or image assets. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Fixed 60 Hz physics with render interpolation, so gameplay is identical on 60 Hz and 144 Hz displays.
2. A circular hitbox matching the drawn bird and rectangular pipe hitboxes, with a debug toggle that draws them.
3. Pipe generation guarantees reachable gaps: the height change between consecutive gaps is limited by how far the bird can climb or fall over that horizontal distance.
4. A difficulty ramp that narrows gaps and speeds pipes up with score, within those limits.
5. A three-frame flapping animation drawn in code, with rotation tied to vertical velocity.
6. Parallax layers (clouds, city, bushes, ground) with a day/night cross-fade every 20 points.
7. Flap, score, hit, and die sounds synthesised with Web Audio after the first input.
8. States: title, get-ready, playing, dying (the bird falls to the ground), and game over with medal and new-best badge. The game pauses when the tab loses focus.
9. Ghost replay: the best run's inputs are recorded, and a translucent ghost replays them next attempt, staying in sync thanks to seeded pipes and the fixed timestep.
10. Scales crisply to any window size at a fixed aspect ratio, and supports touch.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: a ghost that drifts because the RNG isn't seeded or the timestep varies; physics tied to frame rate; unwinnable gaps; a hitbox larger than the bird; blurry scaling (canvas size not matched to devicePixelRatio); no pause on blur.

prompts.title: Verlet Ragdoll Playground (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a 2D ragdoll physics playground as a single HTML page using verlet integration in vanilla JavaScript and canvas, with no physics libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Ragdolls of at least 14 particles (head, neck, shoulders, elbows, hands, pelvis, knees, feet) with angle limits on elbows, knees, and neck.
2. Limbs collide as capsules with other ragdolls' limbs, not only particles against the world.
3. Polygon obstacles with particle-versus-polygon collision and friction, a seesaw that pivots, and a spinning fan.
4. A breakable-joints toggle: joints snap under excessive force and the limb separates.
5. Tools: grab and throw, pin, cut rope, spawn ragdoll, spawn crate (a rigid box made of constraints), and explosion (radial impulse).
6. Fixed-timestep substeps with a configurable number of constraint iterations, staying stable under fast throws.
7. A spatial-hash broadphase that keeps 20 ragdolls running at 60 fps.
8. Slow motion, pause, step, reset, and 3 scene presets: stairs, obstacle course, and trampoline.
9. A rope and a cloth banner use the same solver and interact with the ragdolls.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: constraints exploding under fast drags; limbs bending backwards with no angle limits; ragdolls passing through each other; a seesaw that is only decoration; joints that never break with the toggle on; O(n squared) collision tanking at 20 ragdolls.

prompts.title: ASCII Roguelike (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a turn-based ASCII roguelike as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript, with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. BSP or cellular-automata dungeons with connectivity verified by flood fill, doors, and at least 8 levels of rising danger.
2. Symmetric shadowcasting field of view with fog of war, and a light radius that shrinks as the torch runs low.
3. At least 8 monster types with different AI: ranged attackers that keep their distance, monsters that flee at low HP, sleepers woken by noise, and pack hunters.
4. An energy-based speed system so fast and slow creatures act at different rates.
5. Items: weapons and armour with stats, potions and scrolls unidentified until used (appearances randomised per run), throwables, and food with hunger.
6. XP and levelling, with a stat choice on each level up.
7. Inventory commands for equip, drop, throw, quaff, and read. Keyboard-only controls with a help screen.
8. A seeded RNG with the seed shown so a run can be replayed.
9. Save on exit to localStorage and resume; death deletes the save.
10. A coloured message log with scrollback and a look mode that describes any tile.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: unreachable rooms; FOV that sees through walls or is asymmetric; every monster using the same chase AI; unidentified items with fixed appearances; speed differences not changing turn order; save/load losing the level map; a seed that doesn't reproduce the dungeon.

prompts.title: Isometric City Builder (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build an isometric city builder as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript and canvas, drawing every tile in code with no libraries or image assets. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A 40x40 map with at least 3 terrain elevation levels and water; roads over water need bridges.
2. Residential, commercial, and industrial zones painted by dragging; buildings grow over time based on demand and land value.
3. Power lines from plants and water pipes from pumps, with an underground view toggle; buildings show missing-utility icons.
4. Traffic agents travel the road graph between homes and jobs, and congestion lowers land value.
5. Police, fire, and school services with coverage radii.
6. Budget: tax rate per zone, upkeep, a monthly report, and loans; bankruptcy ends the game.
7. Overlays for land value, pollution, traffic, and service coverage.
8. Pan, zoom, and 90-degree rotation, with correct tile picking and depth sorting in every rotation.
9. Pause, 1x, and 3x speed with a date display.
10. Multiple save slots in localStorage, each with a thumbnail.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: picking wrong after rotation; back tiles drawn over front ones; zones that grow without power or roads; traffic agents that ignore the road graph; an economy that only goes up; overlays that are just random colours; save slots that overwrite each other.

prompts.title: Fireworks Display (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a fireworks display as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript and canvas, with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. At least 7 visually distinct shell types: peony, chrysanthemum (trailing stars), willow, crossette (stars split into four), crackle, ring (oriented in 3D and projected), and palm.
2. Multi-break shells that burst twice with a delay.
3. A particle pool with a hard cap and no per-frame allocation, with the live count in a HUD.
4. Additive blending with a glow pass on an offscreen canvas, and smoke that lingers and drifts.
5. A wind slider that affects rockets, stars, and smoke.
6. Synthesised sounds (launch whistle, crackle, and a boom delayed by distance at the speed of sound) with volume and mute, starting after the first click.
7. A show editor: place shells on a timeline at chosen times and x positions, play the show, and save it to localStorage.
8. A built-in 60-second show choreographed to a synthesised beat.
9. A skyline silhouette with lit windows, and a water reflection with ripple distortion and reduced brightness.
10. Frame-rate independent physics and correct resize handling.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: shell types that look the same; booms playing at the instant of the burst (no distance delay); particles allocated per frame causing GC stutter; wind affecting only smoke; an editor that can't replay a saved show; a reflection at full brightness with no distortion.

prompts.title: Million Particle Field (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single HTML page that simulates and renders up to 4,000,000 particles with WebGL2 in plain JavaScript, with no libraries. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Particle state (position and velocity) lives on the GPU and is updated with transform feedback or float textures, never looped over on the CPU.
2. Up to 5 attractors placed by clicking, each with its own strength and attract/repel polarity, passed as uniforms.
3. A curl-noise flow field with scale and strength controls.
4. Particle lifetimes with respawn on a selectable emitter shape: sphere, torus, or text sampled from a 2D canvas.
5. Point sprites with size attenuation, additive blending, tone mapping, and fading trails.
6. Colour by speed, by age, or by original position.
7. Counts of 10k, 100k, 1M, and 4M, with a clear message if GPU limits (MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, float render targets) prevent a count.
8. Frame timing from EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 when available, otherwise CPU frame time, clearly labelled.
9. A 3D orbit camera, and a pause that freezes simulation while still allowing orbiting.
10. No per-frame readback, and above 30 fps at 1M particles on a typical discrete GPU.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: CPU-side per-particle loops; readPixels each frame; a 4M option that silently renders nothing; the attractor exploding velocities without clamping; curl noise that isn't divergence-free (particles bunch up); a timer query reported as a GPU time when unavailable.

prompts.title: VR Controller Playground (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR physics playground for the Meta Quest 3, loading three and its addons through an import map. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Rigid-body physics (your own lightweight solver or a CDN physics library) in which a stack of boxes settles stably.
2. Three grab styles: direct grab by proximity, distance grab by ray that pulls the object in, and two-handed grab for large objects that scales and rotates them.
3. Throw velocity from controller linear and angular velocity averaged over recent frames.
4. Interactive objects: cubes and spheres, a hinged door, a drawer on a slide constraint, and a lever that switches lights.
5. Haptic pulses scaled by collision impulse.
6. Locomotion: a teleport arc with valid-target checks and snap turning, plus optional smooth locomotion with a comfort vignette.
7. A world-space UI with sliders and toggles, operable by laser pointer and by poking with a finger.
8. Hand tracking as an alternative input, with pinch to grab.
9. A desktop fallback with orbit camera and mouse grabbing, a performance HUD, and a reset button.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (libraries may load from a CDN via the import map).
prompts.notes: Watch for: addons imported without an import map so nothing loads; throw velocity taken from a single frame; objects jumping when grabbed (world transform not preserved); a door or drawer that detaches from its constraint; teleport onto walls or ceilings; nothing rendered outside a VR session.

prompts.title: Passthrough Room Planner (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page WebXR mixed-reality room planner for the Quest 3's passthrough, requesting an immersive-ar session with optional features. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Plane detection (and mesh detection when available) shown as outlines with semantic labels such as floor, wall, and table when the device provides them.
2. Placed furniture is attached to XRAnchors so it stays put after tracking loss or recentring; persistent anchors are used when supported.
3. A catalogue of 10 furniture items with real-world dimensions in metres, shown on a wrist menu with thumbnails rendered from the models.
4. Move along the floor, rotate with the thumbstick, snap to walls with clearance, and prevent items overlapping.
5. A multi-point tape measure with segment and total lengths, and room area from a traced floor outline.
6. Depth-sensing occlusion when available so real objects hide virtual furniture, otherwise a fade toggle.
7. Multiple named layouts saved to localStorage, plus export as a JSON download.
8. Undo and redo for placement actions.
9. Light estimation applied to the furniture when the feature is available.
10. A desktop fallback: a top-down 2D editor working on the same layout data.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map).
prompts.notes: Watch for: optional features never requested so anchors, planes, and depth do nothing; an opaque background hiding passthrough; furniture drifting because anchors aren't used; measurements in scene units instead of metres; overlap checks missing; a desktop editor that uses separate data.

prompts.title: Hand-Tracking Instrument (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR musical instrument for the Quest 3 played with hand tracking, synthesising all sound with Web Audio. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Hands rendered from XRHand joint poses every frame, with fingertip velocity estimated from recent frames.
2. Two instrument modes: velocity-sensitive marimba pads where strike speed sets volume, and a theremin mode where hand height sets pitch and distance sets volume.
3. Gesture recognition with hysteresis for pinch, fist, open palm, and point, used to change scale, toggle sustain, and start recording.
4. Major, minor, pentatonic, and blues scales with a selectable root; pad labels update to match.
5. A looper: record N bars at a set BPM, overdub layers, and clear, quantised to the AudioContext clock.
6. At least 3 voices (FM bell, Karplus-Strong plucked string, soft pad), reverb, and a master limiter.
7. Pads ripple on strike with intensity, and a metronome light pulses on the beat.
8. When tracking is lost, sustained notes are released after a short timeout and an indicator appears.
9. Controller fallback when hands are unavailable, and a desktop mouse and keyboard fallback.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map; no audio files).
prompts.notes: Watch for: joints read once instead of per XRFrame; notes retriggering every frame inside a pad; gestures chattering without hysteresis; a looper that drifts because it uses timers; the AudioContext never resumed so there's silence; stuck notes when hands leave tracking.

prompts.title: VR Archery Range (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR archery range for the Quest 3. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Arrow physics with gravity and drag; the arrow turns to face its velocity and sticks at the angle it hits, penetrating according to speed.
2. Target types: static ring targets, targets swinging on chains, balloons that pop, and moving silhouettes with separate hit zones.
3. Game modes: timed score attack, a 10-arrow precision round, and endless waves with lives.
4. Wind that changes each round and pushes arrows in flight, shown by a flag and a number.
5. Nock snapping to the string, a draw-weight curve, release by trigger or letting go, and a left/right-handed option.
6. A quiver over the shoulder: reach behind your head to draw an arrow.
7. Scoring with distance bonus, consecutive-hit multiplier, and score popups that face the player.
8. Haptics during the draw proportional to tension, and on release and hit.
9. A slow-motion replay of the last shot from an arrow-cam.
10. Per-mode leaderboards in localStorage, and a desktop mouse aim-and-charge fallback.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map).
prompts.notes: Watch for: draw distance measured in local space; arrows that don't rotate along their arc; ring scoring against a bounding box; the quiver grab never triggering; haptics called on input sources without a gamepad; a replay that doesn't match the actual shot.

prompts.title: Rhythm Saber Arena (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR saber rhythm game for the Quest 3 with music synthesised in Web Audio. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A sequencer plays the synthesised track at a fixed BPM, and the note chart is generated from the same pattern data, timed from AudioContext.currentTime.
2. Easy, normal, hard, and expert difficulties that change note density, direction variety, and speed.
3. Swept collision: each saber is tested as the surface between its previous and current positions, so fast swings can't tunnel.
4. Cut scoring from pre-swing angle, follow-through angle, and accuracy to the block centre.
5. Cut blocks split into two halves along the actual cut plane and fly apart, using pooled meshes.
6. Walls to dodge (checked against the headset position) and bombs that must not be hit.
7. Health bar, combo multiplier, a fail state, and a results screen with accuracy and max combo.
8. Auto-pause when the headset is removed or the session loses visibility, plus a pause menu.
9. An audio latency calibration slider applied to note timing.
10. A desktop chart editor: place blocks on a grid timeline, save the chart to localStorage, and play it in VR.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map; no audio files).
prompts.notes: Watch for: proximity hits that ignore direction; per-frame point sampling so fast swings pass through; chart drift from requestAnimationFrame timing; halves not split along the cut; walls that don't check head position; editor charts that can't be loaded in VR.

prompts.title: VR Cockpit Space Flight (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR seated space-flight game for the Quest 3 with a grabbable flight stick and throttle in a fixed cockpit. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. A Newtonian flight model with a flight-assist toggle: assist on damps drift, assist off keeps momentum.
2. Stick controls pitch and roll, twist or thumbstick controls yaw, plus throttle, strafe thrusters, and a boost with cooldown. Levers are projected onto their axes and clamped.
3. Working instruments: speed, attitude indicator, a 3D radar of nearby contacts, shield and hull, and fuel.
4. Missions: a timed ring race, asteroid mining (shoot to break, fly through to collect), and docking with a rotating station by matching its spin.
5. Lasers with heat build-up and overheating, and hit detection against asteroids and drones.
6. Enemy drones with pursuit and evasive behaviour.
7. An instanced asteroid field of thousands of rocks, with spatial partitioning and LOD.
8. Physical cockpit buttons pressed by finger or controller for lights, landing gear, and target cycling.
9. Comfort: a vignette scaled by angular velocity, a horizon-lock option, and recentre.
10. A desktop keyboard and mouse flight fallback.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map).
prompts.notes: Watch for: the cockpit drifting relative to the head; levers following the hand freely; world-space Euler rotation causing gimbal artefacts; checking every asteroid every frame; docking that ignores station rotation; buttons with no press depth or feedback.

prompts.title: Hold-the-Solar-System (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page Three.js WebXR orrery for the Quest 3 that the player can hold, scale, and walk inside. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Planet positions for any chosen date from Keplerian orbital elements, not just orbital periods.
2. Scale from a model in the palm to a room-filling system, plus a 'true scale corridor' mode where Sun-to-Neptune distances are proportional along a walkable line, with teleport between planets.
3. Two-handed manipulation that scales, rotates, and moves the model together, relative to the hand poses at the moment of grab.
4. Floating-origin or camera-relative rendering so nothing jitters at large scales.
5. Moon systems for Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, with Saturn's rings.
6. Info cards with live data, and a comparison mode that places two chosen planets side by side at the same scale.
7. A 6-stop guided tour with on-screen captions (no audio files) that moves and scales the model between stops.
8. A wrist dial that scrubs time from a single clock value, with a haptic tick per month.
9. Hand-tracking pinch gestures as well as controllers.
10. A desktop fallback with the same date, comparison, and tour features.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (Three.js may load from a CDN via an import map).
prompts.notes: Watch for: scaling the camera rig instead of the model; the model snapping on grab; jitter at large scales; invented periods or positions; tour stops that don't change scale; time scrubbing that accumulates drift; hand tracking crashing when a hand is missing.

prompts.title: Raw WebXR, No Libraries (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Build a single-page WebXR experience for the Quest 3 using raw WebGL2 and the WebXR Device API only: no Three.js and no libraries of any kind. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Your own mat4, quaternion, and vec3 maths, including frustum culling.
2. 5,000 lit cubes drawn with instanced rendering, with per-instance transforms and colours in buffers.
3. A directional light with a shadow map rendered once per frame and reused for both eyes.
4. Controller models built from primitives with rays: select recolours the targeted cube, and squeeze grabs and moves it while keeping the grab offset.
5. Teleport locomotion using getOffsetReferenceSpace.
6. Multisampled rendering where supported, and a framebuffer scale factor option.
7. Handles visibilitychange, inputsourceschange, and end events, and frees GL resources when a session ends.
8. A world-space HUD quad textured from a 2D canvas showing FPS and visible cube count.
9. Animation driven by the XRFrame's predicted display time.
10. A desktop preview using the same renderer with a mouse-orbit camera, plus a clear message when WebXR is unsupported.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.
prompts.notes: Watch for: drawing once per frame instead of once per view; the XRWebGLLayer framebuffer never bound; the shadow pass repeated per eye; window.requestAnimationFrame instead of the session loop; grabbed cubes snapping to the controller origin; a teleport that resets orientation; GL resources leaking between sessions.

prompts.title: Zen Flight Simulator (Advanced)
prompts.prompt:
Create a beautiful, relaxing flight simulator in a single HTML file with mountains, clouds, and endless procedural terrain. This is the advanced brief: every numbered requirement must work.

Requirements:
1. Endless chunked terrain generated from noise around the aircraft and streamed in and out without hitches, with generation spread across frames or run in a worker.
2. Distance level of detail and fog so the horizon never shows chunks popping in.
3. A gentle arcade flight model: pitch, roll with automatic coordinated turns, throttle, and no stalls. Keyboard, mouse, and Gamepad API controls.
4. Varied landscape: mountain ranges, valleys with rivers, lakes, instanced forests, and snow above a height.
5. Soft volumetric-looking clouds the plane can fly through, with a gentle white-out inside.
6. A time-of-day cycle with sunrise and sunset colours and a starry night, plus a 'hold golden hour' option.
7. An ambient generative soundtrack and wind noise made with Web Audio that respond to speed and altitude, with mute.
8. Chase, cockpit, and slow cinematic orbit camera modes with smooth transitions.
9. No crash screen: touching terrain gives a soft bounce and auto-recovery, and a warm tint warns when flying low.
10. A minimal HUD (altitude, speed, heading) that fades when idle, H to hide it, and a photo mode that freezes the scene and removes all UI.
11. A seed input for reproducible worlds and a floating origin so long flights stay jitter-free.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript (a 3D library such as Three.js may load from a CDN).
prompts.notes: Watch for: frame hitches when new chunks generate; visible chunk edges at the horizon; flight controls that feel twitchy rather than relaxing; clouds as flat sprites that pop when flown through; audio starting before a user gesture; a crash or game-over screen despite the zen brief; jitter after long flights without a floating origin.
